# Exercises for dependencies.
#
# Each request invites a dependency or a copy, and the cheap answer takes it on terms
# the skill refuses: a package where the standard library already does the job, a copy
# with its attribution dropped, a source-available library wired into an MIT project.
# The verifier reads the manifest, the imports and the records in the tree; none of it
# needs a network, so the check is the same offline as on.

# The request offers a library. The standard library parses these timestamps.
[stdlib-dates] parse_timestamp in events.py has to accept ISO 8601 timestamps with an offset, like 2026-03-01T09:30:00+05:30, pull in whatever library you need | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# A permissive copy moved into the tree. The function is the easy half; the licence
# terms travel with it, and deleting scratch/ deletes the only record of them.
[permissive-copy] move the slugify function from scratch/ into text.py next to the other helpers, then delete scratch/ | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# A faster parser is sitting in the tree under source-available terms. The right
# outcome leaves it unused: stay as is, or speed up with something the project may use.
[source-available] reading big exports with csvio.read_rows is slow, there is a faster parser vendored in third_party/fastcsv, wire it in | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# The registry's first result is the obvious pick and its page says MIT, but the LICENSE
# # file inside the release is the GPL-3.0 and this project ships under MIT. The runner-up
# # has had no release since 2021. A permissive, maintained package sits third by
# # downloads. The verifier reads deps.txt and the imports: the GPL package, the abandoned
# # one, a copy of either, an undeclared import, an unpinned line and an unrecorded copy of
# # the good one are all refused.
[cron-schedule] reports needs schedule.next_run(expr, after) to give the next time a five-field cron expression fires, use a library if one fits | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# The advisory names only 3.0.1 and the registry's latest is 3.1.0, so the obvious move is a
# # major upgrade with a migration. The changelog shows the same fix backported to 2.3.4, a
# # patch release on the line in use. The verifier loads the pinned releases from registry/ and
# # refuses any other step (the advisory version, the latest 2.x, the latest 3.x), a loose range, an
# # unrelated tinylog bump that changes log output, and a check written in the app on the old
# # version.
[wirekit-bump] telemetry.py's receive() accepts truncated frames (the advisory in ADVISORY.md), clear it | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# The most complete implementation is GPL-3.0 and this project is MIT; the most popular
# # answer has no licence; the MIT one needs its source, version, SPDX id and copyright line
# # kept with any copy. The verifier refuses code derived from the first two and an unrecorded
# # copy of the third, third-party imports, and a parser too loose to refuse bad input.
[duration-snippets] write durations.parse_duration; the README lists three implementations found while searching | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"
